title: Beef and Rice Stuffed Peppers with Tomato and Melted Cheese
summary: Sweet red or yellow peppers packed with a savoury filling of browned beef, rice, tomato and mozzarella, glazed with a tangy tomato topping and baked until the cheese is golden. A complete, family-friendly dinner in one dish.
equipment: baking dish that holds the peppers upright snugly (about 23 cm square)

ingredients.item: large red or yellow peppers (about 200 g each)
tin chopped tomatoes (no salt added), drained, 60 ml juice kept

ingredients.note: 80 g for the filling, 20 g for the top

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare the peppers
steps.text: Slice 1 cm off the top of each pepper and pull out the core and seeds. Bring the large saucepan of unsalted water to the boil, add the peppers and cook for 3 minutes until they just start to soften. Lift them out with the slotted spoon and stand them upside down to drain; a brief blanch gives them a head start so they become tender in the oven at the same time as the filling heats through.

steps.title: Boil the rice
steps.text: Bring the same water back to the boil, add the rice and boil for 12-13 minutes until just tender. Drain it well in the sieve and tip it into the large bowl. Slightly firm rice is ideal here, as it finishes softening in the oven by soaking up the tomato juices.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Warm the oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and beginning to brown. Add the beef and cook for 5-6 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until browned all over with no raw red bits left (ground meat 71 °C). Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds; added last, it releases its aroma without burning.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Add the beef mixture to the rice along with the drained tomatoes, 80 g of the mozzarella, the parsley, salt and pepper, and mix thoroughly. The cheese melts as it bakes and binds the rice and meat so the filling holds together when you cut into it.

steps.title: Fill and top
steps.text: Stand the peppers snugly in the baking dish and pack the filling in firmly, mounding it slightly at the top. Stir the ketchup into the kept tomato juice, spoon it over each pepper and scatter over the remaining mozzarella. A snug dish keeps the peppers upright so the filling stays inside.

steps.title: Bake and rest
steps.text: Bake for 25-30 minutes until the cheese is browned, the peppers are tender when pierced with a knife and the centre of the filling reads 74 °C. Rest for 5 minutes before serving so the juices settle and the filling firms slightly.

tips: A common mistake is salting the blanching water; the outline keeps it unsalted because the filling is already seasoned, so leave the salt out.
Choose peppers with flat bases so they stand up on their own; if one wobbles, shave a thin slice off the bottom without cutting through.
Check the centre of the filling with a probe thermometer rather than relying on the browned cheese, which colours before the middle is hot.
Low-moisture mozzarella melts without making the filling watery, so avoid fresh mozzarella balls here.
storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour and use within 24 hours. Reheat once, covered, until piping hot (74 °C) throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
